entry.title: Social Summary: September 24, 2026
entry.summary: Launch of the week — Bot Screen / Hermes Desktop: The clear headline is @NousResearch's flagship Bot Screen announcement — live-streaming any agent's session with interactive takeover via Hermes Desktop (score 98, highest engagement in the batch). @Teknium followed with a first-party post on live desktop passthrough to the same machine the Hermes Agent runs on, and the official account amplified @tonbistudio's walkthrough video plus docs (with a @Teknium boost of the guide video). Sentiment is emphatically positive and anticipatory: @Teknium's 'Finallllly!' and 'Much needed!' (203 likes) frame it as a long-awaited ship, and @NousResearch's 'This is the way' reply kept the tone celebratory. Community OSS — the Jev ecosystem: @rlaope's oh-my-hermes (OMH) plugin gained Jev-Skills, Jev models/aliases, and model routing, positioning OMH as the all-in-one plugin for hermes-agent power users, alongside the newly open-sourced jeval evaluation/visualization tool (near-duplicate share excluded) — a sign of grassroots momentum around Jev fast decision-making in Hermes workflows. Maintainer engagement: Core-team responsiveness is a strong secondary thread — @Teknium firmly disputed a cache-bug claim and routed it to the issue tracker, fixed a user-reported issue same-day, and corrected attribution that the disputed tooling was built by @NousResearch, not Anthropic. Overall read: a confident, fast-moving maintainer presence and a hype-filled, well-received launch week. Tips & low-signal chatter: A practical Hermes via iMessage tip with model flexibility is a nice newsletter tidbit; the remainder (emoji-only replies, 'I agree', link-only OMH post, GitHub engagement bait, and an off-topic take on Claude Opus 5.5 vs Claude Code) is positive but low-information and was deprioritized.

entry.title: You can now watch your agents work live as Hermes Desktop streams the screen of any bot's screen or ...
entry.summary: NousResearch announces the Bot Screen feature: Hermes Desktop can stream any bot's screen or session in real time, letting users watch agents drive a browser, type into a terminal, or open windows, and take over interactively to enter credentials before handing back control.
